### Sankey chart
Flows between nodes, each link as thick as its value.

Runtime ownership: `auto-init`. No dedicated entry in the reviewed Google component inventory.

Example: Energy from solar, wind and gas through the grid to homes and industry is a sankey chart. Visitors leaving at each step of one checkout is a bar chart.

Relationship: none. Web extension; no dedicated entry was observed in the reviewed current M3 component inventory.

Upstream: web-extension-inventory-reviewed (2026-10-25); [evidence](https://m3.material.io/components).

Requirements and boundaries: design reference web-extensions-review. The inventory page renders client-side, so this review relies on the 2026-09-13 inventory review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.

Support (2026-10-25, `llm.md#sankey-chart`): Nodes and links drawn from a figure's data table of source, target and value columns, with nodes in columns by their longest path from a source, stacked in the order they first appear, links and nodes on one scale, rows skipped for values that are not positive, missing names, self links and cycles, node names and colors, right-to-left mirroring, update() motion, data-watch, and a pointer and keyboard tooltip that steps through links in table order.

Web adaptation: The <table> stays in the page as the text alternative and the no-JavaScript fallback; the SVG and node names are aria-hidden and the plot is one Tab stop with a polite live tooltip.

Known boundary: Link and node sizes, columns, skipped rows, names, colors, right-to-left mirroring, keyboard steps, the link under the pointer, update() motion and data-watch are checked in a browser; screen reader output, forced colors and enlarged text remain unverified. Nodes are not reached by keyboard or pointer, and node order follows the table with no crossing reduction.

Full parity remains unassessed. [Capability evidence](../references/capability-roadmap.md#sankey-chart).

#### Contract

A `<figure class="sankey-chart">` takes a `<figcaption>` and a `<table>` with one row per flow. The first column names the flow's source node, the second its target node, and the third holds its value. `AutoInit()` draws the nodes in columns and each row as a link from its source to its target, and a tooltip shows the link under the pointer. The table stays in the page, visually hidden, as the chart's text alternative; without JavaScript it shows instead of the chart.

#### Syntax

```html
<figure class="sankey-chart">
  <figcaption>Energy flow (TWh)</figcaption>
  <table>
    <thead>
      <tr><th>Source</th><th>Target</th><th>TWh</th></tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
      <tr><th>Solar</th><td>Grid</td><td>30</td></tr>
      <tr><th>Wind</th><td>Grid</td><td>50</td></tr>
      <tr><th>Grid</th><td>Homes</td><td>60</td></tr>
      <tr><th>Grid</th><td>Industry</td><td>20</td></tr>
    </tbody>
  </table>
</figure>
```

#### Rules

- `sankey-chart-is-a-figure-with-a-table`: Write .sankey-chart as a <figure> holding a <table> of the flows. The drawn chart is hidden from assistive technology, so the table is all a screen reader reads, and it is what shows without JavaScript.
- `sankey-chart-has-a-caption`: Name a .sankey-chart with a <figcaption>. It names the focusable plot as well as the figure; hide it with .visually-hidden when nearby text already names the chart.
